rows.title: A year after Colorado voters approved Proposition 123, demand for its affordable housing funds outweighs supply
rows.standfirst: More than 200 local governments have pledged to increase their affordable housing stock in the coming years. Now developers are applying for funds to build those units.

rows.title: Women accused of stealing $4.5 million from investors in Idaho Springs resort project indicted on federal charges
rows.standfirst: Money siphoned from an escrow account in the Argo Mill project led federal investigators to nine other victims who allegedly lost $10 million to a Virginia title company scheme

rows.title: What’s Working: Wireless phone bills in Colorado are lower than the national average
rows.standfirst: Inflation is still high, but the mobile service providers say they charge the same price everywhere. What’s the cause? Rising taxes and fees. Plus: Affordable phone plans, more!

rows.title: Tri-State moves up closure of coal burning power plant, lines up for $970M federal grant for wind, solar generation
rows.standfirst: Local utilities leaving the giant electricity producer opened the door to early retirement of Craig Station Unit 3 by start of 2028.

rows.title: Colorado’s runaway truck ramps, fixtures for decades, see renewed focus in campaign for highway safety
rows.standfirst: One man’s failure to use a ramp in 2019 led to state and industry collaboration on raising awareness of the precipitous danger of mountain driving

rows.title: The town of San Luis has received nearly $2 million in revitalization grants since 2019. Will a tourism economy take hold?
rows.standfirst: Town leaders hope the latest $500,000 grant, from the Environmental Protection Agency, will tip the southern Colorado town into tourist friendliness — which some say it needs to survive.

rows.title: Colorado utility bills keep growing even though the price of electricity is static. Here’s why.
rows.standfirst: Since 2019 the average monthly residential bill, for 600 kilowatt-hours of electricity, has risen 38% to $92

rows.title: A Colorado town wants to use geothermal energy to heat and cool a section of its downtown core
rows.standfirst: A geothermal test well drilled in Carbondale with a federal grant yields promising results for next-gen application of ancient technology

rows.title: Frontier Airlines settles lawsuit with Colorado pilots over alleged pregnancy, breastfeeding discrimination
rows.standfirst: The Denver-based airline will become one of the first to allow pilots to pump milk in the cockpit during noncritical phases of the flight

rows.title: A new Colorado film festival brings modern meaning to a historic yellow barn
rows.standfirst: The Yellow Barn Farm just north of Boulder was once a thriving equestrian center. Now it’s an incubation site for all kinds of cultural and agricultural experiments.

rows.title: 24 ideas floated for saving water and protecting Colorado River from drought, climate change
rows.standfirst: Colorado River Drought Task Force has worked up recommendations for protecting rivers and wildlife habitat, fixing leaking water delivery systems and adding flexibility to shared water programs

rows.title: Xcel Energy pitches new clean energy plan for Colorado that is nearly twice as costly as one it offered in 2021
rows.standfirst: Colorado utilities regulators will consider the new plan, which was revised in hopes of capturing lucrative renewable energy credits while slashing greenhouse gas emissions

rows.title: Tents line streets outside hotels — now acting as migrant shelters — as number of Venezuelans arriving in Denver nears 30,000
rows.standfirst: As winter approaches, migrant families no longer have a time limit in shelters, but single adults must move out after 14 days

rows.title: Colorado regulators consider trimming Xcel Energy plan to build new solar, wind generation
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s largest utility is also asking for $3B in new transmission lines. PUC looks to see if that sum can be cut before passing it on to consumers.

rows.title: About 30% of Denver’s downtown office space is vacant — and that doesn’t include “zombie buildings”
rows.standfirst: In the Denver metro, “office” has become a 4-letter word

rows.title: Montanya rum distillery sells to long-time employees as another veteran owner of a Colorado mountain town business walks
rows.standfirst: Karen Hoskin created Montanya Distillers in 2008, building a craft distilling phenomenon. She’s leaving it in the hands of women who helped her get there.

rows.title: Colorado dodged a recession in 2023. But what about in 2024?
rows.standfirst: Economists called the state’s economy resilient but they’re also more pessimistic than they were a year ago. Plus economies around the state and more!

rows.title: Is getting a Christmas tree in Colorado too expensive? It goes back to the Great Recession.
rows.standfirst: Costs of fertilizers, fuel and labor have also continued to increase over the long life of a farmed tree

rows.title: Colorado landlords are skirting a 2021 law meant to protect renters using vouchers, advocates say

rows.title: Thousands of permits designed to protect Colorado streams are expired

rows.title: $1M in grants offered to Colorado farmers with new ideas about conserving water
rows.standfirst: A Colorado agricultural nonprofit is offering $1 million in grants to farmers and ranchers who are looking into the future to find ways to remain productive and profitable while conserving scarce water supplies.

rows.title: $3B trimmed from Xcel Energy’s ambitious plan for new solar, wind electricity generation in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The Public Utilities Commission tapped the brakes on Xcel’s energy resource plan, saying it wanted more information on the costs and timing of new projects.

rows.title: We know there’s a lack of trust in news. So we did something about it.
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun joins The Trust Project to advance trustworthy news by adopting its 8 Trust Indicators, which help readers identify honest journalism and encourage accountability and integrity

rows.title: What’s Working: How a Colorado music festival is cracking down on ticket scalpers

rows.title: Farm to quaff: How a Colorado nonprofit connects beer and spirit lovers to local sources
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Grain Chain works to keep the food chain local, linking local breweries and distilleries with grains grown in-state

rows.title: State board blocks Douglas County’s creative attempt to provide property tax relief to its homeowners
rows.standfirst: Members of the State Board of Equalization said a 4% reduction in Douglas County’s home values was unwarranted and expressed anxiety about how approving the change could set a precedent followed in other parts of the state

rows.title: You think a pound of beef is expensive? Wait until you hear what it costs to produce it in Colorado.
rows.standfirst: Since 2018, the cost of beef has risen 28% at retail — and ranchers are feeling the pinch from all sides.

rows.title: Drought task force has big ideas for the Colorado River, but senator who convened panel questions its work
rows.standfirst: New ideas to help the drought-stressed Colorado River, including big changes to water rights tied to coal-fired power plants in the iconic Yampa River Valley and elsewhere, and new funding for tribal water systems that could bring much-needed flexibility to river management are being offered up by a special task force. rows.title: Outdated hiring practices may keep Colorado’s new tech talent from finding work
rows.standfirst: A talent shortage has been a rallying cry in the tech industry to create a better pipeline. But tech-training programs wonder if the pipeline gets snubbed because of “unnecessary credentials,” like a college degree or experience.

rows.title: Colorado Springs Independent, an alternative weekly newspaper, indefinitely ceases publication
rows.standfirst: For three decades, the progressive weekly provided residents in Colorado’s second-largest city with an alternate source of news from Colorado Springs’ daily newspaper, The Gazette

rows.title: The housing market has buoyed Colorado’s state budget. That may not last.

rows.title: Battle over United Power’s quest to leave Tri-State ends with a federal regulator’s exit formula

rows.title: Who is homeless in Denver? Let’s look at the numbers.
